text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.96% today as oil prices retreated from their recent highs. Crude has dropped from $109+ (mid-October spike driven by Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities) to $101.91 today, easing concerns about immediate supply disruptions in the Middle East. For a refiner, lower oil prices reduce input costs but also compress profit margins — the benefit depends on how quickly refined product prices adjust, and today's move suggests traders are pricing in a temporary easing of geopolitical tension rather than a bullish demand outlook.

The stock is still up 8.5% over two weeks, reflecting the volatility baked into oil refining when geopolitical risk flares. U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with modest crude and product inventories, so the market remains tight, but the sharp pullback from $484 to $469 in the past week shows traders rotating out of the refiner trade as immediate conflict escalation fears fade.
